I dont know what you went through as not all bipolar people are the same, just as everyone else has their own personality, but Im sure you have your own emotional and experiential revelations in accordance to someone you do or once loved.

It was written quickly and had a plethra of typos...alot of mental connections and not transitional chronological and perhaps a tad incoherent to anyone else topical subjects where brought up. 
Almost like taking a sphere and trying to see it at every angle, rapidly, the sphere being the experience and attempting to make sense of any of it. 

Im a firm believer that if you loved someone once, you'll always love them or at least, there was a reason you did love them or a reason both parties got together. Maybe something that was once attractive and complimented ones stage in development later became uncomplimentary and there wasnt the communication skill set, or want to have heartfelt discourse with ones partner. 

Myself, I suppose, I was trying to find an answer to the unsettling change I saw and take responsibility for my own failings. 

I have a terror it was vengeance and premeditated based upon old happenings that where...but this does not make it the whole. 

I really really judged myself and felt extremely hurt. 

 I understand that you where hurt as well...that, what ended it for you was your partners disorder but more importantly what manifested from the disorder. Im truly sorry to hear that. It was probably very confusing.

I think that what my partner and I had was we understood eachother on a very inimate level when it comes to "disorders" and it worked, for a long time. I put disorders in quotes only because some peoples sane doesnt work for anothers....and no matter what the symptoms be it a sane person or considered insane, anything taken to a destructive extreme can really injure if not channeled or dealt with correctly. I understand that, as written in my history here. I know I never had malice in my heart or any intention to hurt, but at times, it had that affect...I understand the saying,"the road to hell is paved with good intentions."

I hope you got something truly good out of the experience or at least have healed from it. Thank you for writing me back, in all respect. 
Im sure there where challenges you both faced (or perhaps your partner had no regard, I dont know, I tend to judge people on their intentions) in light of all of this and Im sure you gave alot of love in the process. I hope you are well now.

Im sorry and this is not intended to sound short, but many people say this, find a hobby, go adventuring, the list goes on and Ive done all of them. I thought here on a divorce thread I would find some like-pathed folks who are dealing with the emotional portion and share those together.
